# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 20 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 20 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_020_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 3, Chapter 12

**1** "Those from the third mountain — full of thorns and briars — who are they?" "These are believers: some are wealthy, and some are deeply involved in business dealings. The briars represent the wealthy; the thorns represent those entangled in various commercial transactions. These do not associate with God's servants — they are choked by their dealings and their riches, cut off from the righteous." **2** "Some of them give to the poor; others share nothing of what they have. Those who give receive salvation; those who refuse to share are rejected." **3** "Those from the fourth mountain — thorny at the top but green below — these are the double-minded, those who are not entirely righteous. They have faith, but also great wealth. For the most part they are unrighteous, but repentance remains open to them because their green portions are not entirely lifeless." **4** "Those from the fifth mountain — green grass but rugged — these are believers who are righteous, but hard-hearted and self-willed. They desire to understand everything, yet they truly understand nothing." **5** "Because of their stubbornness and empty conceit they quarrel among themselves. They think they have mastered all knowledge, but they are the most ignorant of all. Their foolish arrogance has made them evil and caused them to fall away from the truth." **6** "Nevertheless there is repentance for them, since they are not wicked but foolish and without discernment. If they repent they will live to God; but if they do not repent, they will share the company of the women who have done them harm."

---

### Council Notes

Mountains 3-5 describe three types of spiritually compromised but not wholly lost believers:
- **Mountain 3 (thorns/briars):** the wealthy and the commercially entangled — two distinct subgroups
- **Mountain 4 (half-green):** the double-minded — people genuinely trying to hold faith and wealth simultaneously
- **Mountain 5 (rugged green):** the arrogantly ignorant — not evil but foolish and inflated

The thorn imagery echoes the parable of the soils (Mark 4:18-19): "those who hear the word, but the worries of life and the deceitfulness of wealth and the desires for other things choke the word."

The mysterious "women who have done them harm" (v. 6) likely refers to the personified vices — the counterpart to the seven virtues — who will appear later in the Similitudes.
